title.narrative: Emergency NFI assistance to people in shelters affected by hurricane Oscar in Guantanamo province, Cuba

description.narrative: During October 20 and 21, Hurricane Oscar affected the eastern provinces. The associated heavy rains caused heavy flooding and severe damage to infrastructure and the blocking of roads and highways. In the most affected municipalities in the province of Guantánamo, preliminary assessments suggest that the storm severely affected more than 14,300 homes, with more than half of them reporting total to partial roof collapses. The number is expected to increase, as response activities to the most affected territories is still ongoing, due severe infrastructure damage. Authorities' estimations suggest that 7,000 families (28,000 people) had to leave their homes (displaced) due to severe damage to their roofs and the complete destruction of their essential domestic items.Complementing the government and other UN agencies' response efforts, this IOM project seeks to assist 11,700 people with needs of shelter and NFIs. It will provide emergency assistance to affected people in the municipalities of Imías, Baracoa, Maisí and San Antonio del Sur, in Guantanamo Province in the form of essential household items, NFIs. The project seeks to provide a tailored response to the most vulnerable, including people with disabilities and people older than 60 years in need of shelter and NFIs. IOM will support national and local authorities in their response to assist and protect vulnerable groups and restore access to essential goods and services. The emergency assistance package will complement UNDP’s assistance to restore roofs and will help restore dignified living conditions to the affected population. IOM will apply vulnerability criteria in beneficiary selection. IOM will target 11,700 people in shelters situation affected, including people with disabilities, the elderly, women and children, both temporarily housed in collective shelters and with the host community (estimated 92% of IDPs in shelters).
